sentences.text: Welcome to the Slow English Podcast.
I am Emilie, your host.
Today, we are traveling to Sukhothai, a small city in Thailand.
Sukhothai is famous for its history, old temples, and peaceful streets.
Let's explore Sukhothai together.
Part 2 Where is Sukhothai?
Sukhothai is in northern Thailand.
It is about 400 kilometers from Bangkok, the capital.
The city is surrounded by fields, rivers, and small mountains.
It is quiet and perfect for learning about Thailand's history.
Part 3 History of Sukhothai Sukhothai was the first capital of Thailand in the 13th century.
The name means dawn of happiness.
Many kings ruled here, and they built beautiful temples and statues.
The city was important for art, religion, and culture.
Today, you can still see ancient ruins and Buddha statues in the Sukhothai Historical Park.
Part 4 Sukhothai Historical Park The historical park is the main attraction in Sukhothai.
It has temples, ponds, and old walls.
The most famous temple is Wat Mahathat.
You can see the big -seated Buddha statue, which is very peaceful.
You can walk or ride a bicycle in the park.
It is quiet and beautiful, with birds and flowers everywhere.
Part 5 The City of Sukhothai The modern city is small and friendly.
There are markets, small shops, and local restaurants.
People ride bicycles and motorbikes.
The city is calm and easy to walk around.
Part 6 Food in Sukhothai Food in Sukhothai is tasty and simple.
A famous dish is Sukhothai noodles, made with rice noodles, pork, egg, and vegetables.
People also like fried chicken, curry, and fresh fruit.
Street food is very common.
You can try mango with sticky rice.
It is sweet and delicious.
Part 7 The people of Sukhothai People in Sukhothai are friendly and polite.
They speak Thai, and some people speak English for tourists.
Families are important, and many people live near their parents and grandparents.
Life is simple, calm, and connected to traditions.
Part 8 Culture and Festivals Sukhothai has many festivals and celebrations.
The most famous is Loi Krithong, a festival with floating candles on the river.
People also celebrate Songkran, the Thai New Year, by throwing water and having fun.
Traditional music and dance are part of every celebration.
You can see people playing instruments and singing in the streets.
Part 9 Nature Around Sukhothai Sukhothai is surrounded by green fields, rice paddies, and small forests.
You can see farmers working in the fields.
Many birds live in the area, and the rivers are clean and calm.
It is a perfect place for photography, cycling, and enjoying nature.
Part 10 Travel and Tourism You can reach Sukhothai by bus, car, or plane from Bangkok or Chiang Mai.
Many tourists visit for history, culture, and peace.
Local guides help visitors explore the historical park and the city.
Tourism is important for the people of Sukhothai.
It brings jobs and helps protect the city's history.
Part 11 Daily Life in Sukhothai Life in Sukhothai is calm and slow.
People wake up early, go to work or school, and eat breakfast with family.
In the afternoon, children play in the streets.
In the evening, families walk together and people visit markets or temples.
It is a city where life feels simple and natural.
Part 12 Why Sukhothai is Special Sukhothai is not a big city, but it is full of history and beauty.
It combines ancient temples, nature, and calm life perfectly.
It is a place where visitors can feel the past and enjoy the present.
